🚨🇲🇽 <u>Security Cabinet Captures "Isra," a Los Rusos Operator in Mexicali</u>

Mexico's Navy, the SSPC and the National Guard, working from National Intelligence Center (CNI) intel, arrested Israel Leonel Trigueros Muñoz, "Isra," 42, on Boulevard Adolfo López Mateos in Mexicali. He is identified as a regional operator of Los Rusos, the armed wing of the Sinaloa Cartel's Los Mayos faction across the Mexicali Valley and San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora. He was arrested on a kidnapping warrant and is linked to a 2024 armed attack on a state intelligence official and to the August kidnapping of corridos singer "Gordo Gadaffi."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Alito Moreno vs. the Man With a Phone</u>

PRI leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno lost his temper in Ensenada, Baja California, when a citizen filming him called him "Vandalito," "a disgrace to Mexico" and a "thief." Alito answered "you're sent by Morena" and, with two PRI companions, went for the man's phone. Where it happened: outside the home of former PAN governor Ernesto Ruffo Appel, who is under house arrest while being investigated for organized crime and fuel smuggling. Ruffo had just joined Alito and Vicente Fox on a video call to plan a "grand opposition coalition."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Jalisco Water Protesters Take Their Abuse Claims to the FGR</u>

At least 10 people detained at the October 11 march for clean water in Guadalajara have filed complaints with Mexico's Attorney General's Office (FGR), asking it to take the case away from Jalisco's state authorities. They describe beatings, a woman being choked, forced partial nudity and threats from state police inside Casa Jalisco, Governor Pablo Lemus's residence. Lawyer Adriana Arriola was held there with her 19-year-old daughter. Police told them, "We're going to make you disappear." Their demand is clean water from the tap, and they want Lemus and his security secretary prosecuted.
banner: JALISCO PROTESTERS: ABUSE CASE TO FGR

🇲🇽🐄 <u>Mexican Cattle Cross Again at Puerto Palomas</u>

Mexico resumed live-cattle exports to the US through Puerto Palomas, Chihuahua, on Monday, sending a first 750 head to Columbus, New Mexico, El Financiero reports. It is the third crossing back in business after the US screwworm restrictions, after Agua Prieta, Sonora, and San Jerónimo, Chihuahua. Exports now average about 3,500 head a day, and Agriculture expects Nogales, Sonora, to reopen by the end of November.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Canacar Said No to Segob, Yes to Alito</u>

Days before Monday's highway blockades, Canacar's leadership sat down with PRI national leader Alejandro "Alito" Moreno to discuss "the challenges facing the sector." Then, while most transport organizations accepted the government's call to dialogue, Canacar's leaders kept their strike on. El Soberano reads it as a political agenda riding on a fight over a toll tax break that touches only 170 large companies.

🇲🇽🚚 <u>Most Truckers Chose the Table Over the Blockade</u>

While Canacar kept its national strike going on Monday, Canapat, Conatram and the ANTP, all affiliated with Concamin, rejected the highway blockades and agreed to talks with the government. Finance Secretary Édgar Amador, Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez, SICT officials and National Guard highway commanders committed to a work agenda this week, federal and state, on security, infrastructure, tolls, tax incentives, irregular transport and abuses by authorities. Segob's line: "it is not necessary to resort to blockades to raise demands."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico City Will Host the World Urban Forum in 2028</u>

UN-Habitat executive director Anaclaudia Rossbach announced that Mexico City will host the 14th World Urban Forum, from July 31 to August 4, 2028. She said the choice recognizes the capital's policies on housing, sustainable mobility, public care systems, democratic public space and green-area recovery, and gave Mayor Clara Brugada a Scroll of Honour for her "visionary and participatory" urban regeneration. The forum comes to a world where nearly 3 billion people lack adequate housing and more than 1 billion live in informal settlements.
banner: CDMX TO HOST WORLD URBAN FORUM 2028

🇲🇽🏫 <u>Teachers Get the Vote on USICAMM</u>

Mexico's Education Ministry has called a national consultation of teachers on October 30 to replace USICAMM, the system that controls teacher hiring, promotions and incentives. It fills the whole second School Technical Council session of the year, with online voting open through November 1. ANUIES will send 2,200 university professors to observe in 1,105 schools. Results come out November 5 and will be the basis of the reform the government presents in November, fulfilling Sheinbaum's Commitment 27.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The INE's Favorite Supplier Didn't Start With Taddei</u>

The companies tied to José Alfredo Hernández Casillas, the electoral-materials supplier at the center of the audit that brought down INE chief Guadalupe Taddei, were winning contracts long before she arrived in 2023. La Jornada counts at least 49 contracts from the INE and state electoral bodies between 2018 and 2025, worth 1.45 billion pesos, for ballot boxes, ballots and voting booths. It started under Peña Nieto, with Lorenzo Córdova running the INE. One firm alone, Cajas Graf, took about 656.6 million pesos. The ASF found simulated agreements, triangulated funds, conflicts of interest and dealings with shell companies.
📸 Concurso Nacional de Coros Escolares — Palacio Nacional, Ciudad de México, 26 de octubre de 2026
